sentences.en: Oh, Mrs Patmore, have you heard news?
sentences.zh: 噢，帕特莫太太，你听到消息了吗？

sentences.en: The young master's come back from First World War, and he's had his knackers shot off.
sentences.zh: 那位少爷从一战战场回来了，结果命根子被炸没了。

sentences.en: Oh, now, Daisy, we'll be having none of that talk.
sentences.zh: 噢，黛西，我们可不兴说这种话。

sentences.en: Not when you've got 748 dirty pots to scour before bedtime.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在睡前还有748个脏锅要刷的时候。

sentences.en: Wise words, Mrs Patmore.
sentences.zh: 说得对，帕特莫太太。

sentences.en: Oh, Mr Carson, I didn't see you there.
sentences.zh: 噢，卡森先生，我没看见你在这儿。

sentences.en: There'll be no talk of knackers at Downton Abbey.
sentences.zh: 唐顿庄园里不许谈论什么命根子。

sentences.en: His lordship would not approve.
sentences.zh: 老爷是不会赞同的。

sentences.en: And anyway, young master hasn't had his knackers shot off.
sentences.zh: 再说，那位少爷的命根子根本没被炸掉。

sentences.en: He's paralysed below waiSt.
sentences.zh: 他只是腰部以下瘫痪了。

sentences.en: Not so, Carson.
sentences.zh: 并非如此，卡森。

sentences.en: Lady Mary!
sentences.zh: 玛丽小姐！

sentences.en: Cousin Matthew has made a miraculous recovery, just in time to propose marriage to me in the Christmas special.
sentences.zh: 马修表哥奇迹般地康复了，正好赶在圣诞特辑里向我求婚。

sentences.en: That is wonderful news, my lady.
sentences.zh: 那真是太棒的消息了，小姐。

sentences.en: And I just hope he doesn't then die, so he can stop being on ITV and go to Hollywood.
sentences.zh: 我只希望他别在那之后就死掉，这样他就能离开独立电视台去好莱坞发展了。

sentences.en: Amen, Carson.
sentences.zh: 阿门，卡森。

sentences.en: That, Dominic Sandbrook, was, of course, authentic dialogue from Downton Abbey, the ITV smash hit drama that was a huge success all around the world.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克·桑德布鲁克，刚才那段当然是出自《唐顿庄园》的真实台词，这部独立电视台的热门剧集在全世界都取得了巨大成功。

sentences.en: And it dramatized the world of the Edwardian stately home, didn't it?
sentences.zh: 它戏剧化地呈现了爱德华时代的庄园生活，不是吗？

sentences.en: So upstairs, the Earl of Grantham and his family, including the beautiful Lady Mary, and below stairs with Daisy, the scullery maid who we heard there,
sentences.zh: 楼上住着格兰瑟姆伯爵一家，包括美丽的玛丽小姐；楼下则有我们刚才听到的洗碗女佣黛西，

sentences.en: Mrs Patmore, the myopic cook, and Carson, the stentorially splendid butler.
sentences.zh: 还有近视的厨娘帕特莫太太，以及嗓音洪亮、气派十足的管家卡森。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，大家好。

sentences.en: Secondly, I am so, so sorry.
sentences.zh: 其次，我真的非常、非常抱歉。

sentences.en: Whether you like Downton Abbey or whether you hate it, I hope you're still listening.
sentences.zh: 无论你喜欢还是讨厌《唐顿庄园》，希望你们还在听。

sentences.en: We will be having stern words, the rest is history,
sentences.zh: 我们之后会严肃讨论一下，剩下的就是历史了，

sentences.en: about that conduct.
sentences.zh: 关于那种行为。

sentences.en: So, Tom, you're a great Downton Abbey fan, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，你是《唐顿庄园》的忠实粉丝，对吧？

sentences.en: It started, I think, in 2010.
sentences.zh: 我想它是从2010年开始播出的。

sentences.en: I absolutely love it.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢它。

sentences.en: Do you know, you're a great fan as well, I believe, of the historian Simon Sharma, aren't you, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我相信你也是历史学家西蒙·沙玛的忠实粉丝，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do you know what Simon Sharma said about Downton Abbey?
sentences.zh: 你知道西蒙·沙玛是怎么评价《唐顿庄园》的吗？

sentences.en: Did he not like it?
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢吗？

sentences.en: He said it was a steaming silvered tureen of snobbery, servicing the instincts of cultural necrophilia.
sentences.zh: 他说那是一锅热气腾腾、镀银的势利汤，迎合了文化恋尸癖的本能。

sentences.en: So he likes it, too.
sentences.zh: 所以他也喜欢这部剧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, clearly.
sentences.zh: 没错，显然是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, that's absolutely the point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这正是重点所在。

sentences.en: I have to confess, I don't want to alienate our listeners, but I'm not a massive admirer of Downton Abbey.
sentences.zh: 我得承认，我不想疏远我们的听众，但我实在不是《唐顿庄园》的忠实粉丝。

sentences.en: I think I may have described it to you in a text as one of the worst things I've ever seen.
sentences.zh: 我想我可能在短信里跟你说过，那是我看过最烂的剧之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, you did.
sentences.zh: 没错，你确实说过。

sentences.en: You did.
sentences.zh: 你确实说过。

sentences.en: But, I mean, the ludicrous plots and the hopeless sentimentality of it, it just ticks all my boxes.
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，它那些荒谬的剧情和无可救药的煽情，简直完全戳中了我的点。

sentences.en: However, I am aware that it's not necessarily an accurate portrayal of what life was actually like in an Edwardian stately home.
sentences.zh: 不过，我也知道，它未必真实还原了爱德华时代豪宅里的生活原貌。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, do we have someone who could perhaps lift the veil on what life was actually like?
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，我们有没有人能揭开面纱，讲讲当时的生活到底是什么样的？

sentences.en: We do indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: We do indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: Because, of course, as you said, there's this enduring fascination with the world of the country house, and, in particular, the hierarchical ordered world
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，人们对乡村别墅的世界，尤其是那种等级森严的秩序世界，始终有着持久的迷恋。

sentences.en: of the relationship between masters and servants.
sentences.zh: 也就是主人与仆人之间的关系。

sentences.en: And the best book I've ever read on this, by far, is a book called Servants,
sentences.zh: 关于这个主题，我读过最棒的一本书，遥遥领先，就是那本《仆人》，

sentences.en: A Downstairs View of 20th Century Britain by the historian Lucy Lethbridge.
sentences.zh: 全名是《仆人：二十世纪英国的楼下视角》，由历史学家露西·莱斯布里奇所著。

sentences.en: And this came out about 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这本书大约是十年前出版的。

sentences.en: I reviewed it at the time.
sentences.zh: 我当时还写过书评。

sentences.en: I thought it was wonderful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它写得太棒了。

sentences.en: And we are very honoured, Tom, to have with us on the podcast,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们非常荣幸能在播客中请到一位嘉宾，

sentences.en: Lucy Lethbridge herself.
sentences.zh: 她就是露西·莱斯布里奇本人。

sentences.en: Lucy, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 露西，欢迎来到《历史余韵》节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: And what did you make of Tom's Downton Abbey, may I ask?
sentences.zh: 请问，你对汤姆的《唐顿庄园》有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, I sit somewhere between the two of you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的观点介于你们二位之间。

sentences.en: I was also slightly addicted to it, but also deplored the kind of saccharine coating that it had.
sentences.zh: 我当时也稍微有点上瘾，但同时也对它那种甜腻的包装感到反感。

sentences.en: And the agenda, I think, that it embodied, which was to resurrect the idea that the aristocracy were essentially benign and their servants were sort of happily codependent.
sentences.zh: 我认为它所体现的议程，就是为了重塑这样一种观念：贵族本质上是仁慈的，而他们的仆人则乐于与之共生。

sentences.en: Because I don't think really that was very true.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得那其实并不完全属实。

sentences.en: But it was fun.
sentences.zh: 但那很有趣。

sentences.en: Because, Lucy, that idea, although it's Julian Fellows, isn't it, who's, I mean, he's very into that kind of idea.
sentences.zh: 因为，露西，那个想法，虽然那是朱利安·费罗斯，对吧，我是说，他非常热衷于那种想法。

sentences.en: Conservative peer, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他是保守党贵族。

sentences.en: He is indeed.
sentences.zh: 他确实是。

sentences.en: I mean, with a conservative conservative peer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，和一位保守派的保守党贵族在一起。

sentences.en: And there are actually that many of them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们确实有那么多人。

sentences.en: The idea that he's drawing on is actually one with quite ancient roots in Britain.
sentences.zh: 他所借鉴的理念在英国其实有着相当古老的根源。

sentences.en: The idea that a lord and his servants form a kind of feudal community.
sentences.zh: 即领主和他的仆人构成一种封建共同体的理念。

sentences.en: And it goes right the way back to Middle Ages and names, titles of servants are like butlers, like footmen.
sentences.zh: 这可以一直追溯到中世纪，像管家、男仆这些仆人的称呼和头衔也是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, they go right the way back to the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们确实可以一直追溯到中世纪。

sentences.en: Indeed, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，没错。

sentences.en: But the Victorian and Edwardian household is a sort of recasting of what used to be the kind of rather rollicking entourage that you would get in a medieval feudal household
sentences.zh: 但维多利亚和爱德华时代的家庭，是对中世纪封建家庭中那种相当喧闹的随从群体的一种重塑。

sentences.en: right up to the 18th century, which would be mostly men servants, in fact.
sentences.zh: 一直延续到18世纪，事实上，当时大部分还是男仆。

sentences.en: I mean, there were very few women domestics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时女性仆人非常少。

sentences.en: Most of your entourage would be men.
sentences.zh: 你的随从大多会是男性。

sentences.en: And I think it's a response to social anxiety and to industrialisation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是对社交焦虑和工业化的一种回应。

sentences.en: You get this desire to absolutely fix the hierarchy and you fix it very visibly by having lots of servants in uniforms behind a green bay's door.
sentences.zh: 你会产生一种想要彻底稳固等级制度的渴望，而通过在绿色的双开门后安排大量身着制服的仆人，这种等级感便显得格外显眼。

sentences.en: And it's a very obvious pantomime of the feudal order.
sentences.zh: 这显然是对封建秩序的一种拙劣模仿。

sentences.en: But I think that that appears at a time when there's a lot of anxiety about class.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这出现在人们对阶级感到非常焦虑的时期。

sentences.en: You know, there's a lot of new people stepping into the old estates.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有很多新人搬进了那些老宅区。

sentences.en: There's a lot of new rich.
sentences.zh: 现在有很多新贵。

sentences.en: There's a lot of new middle classes.
sentences.zh: 出现了许多新的中产阶级。

sentences.en: And so this is a necessary, as it were, it's necessary to pretend that these households have the deepest roots, that they're locked into a kind of chivalric ideal.
sentences.zh: 因此，这在某种程度上是必要的，必须假装这些家庭有着最深厚的根基，假装他们被锁定在一种骑士精神的理想之中。

sentences.en: But the actual stately homes, the Downton Abbey equivalents,
sentences.zh: 但那些真正的庄园府邸，也就是《唐顿庄园》里那样的宅邸，

sentences.en: you do get a sense from your book that servants who are working for these houses, they grow up on the estates, they go and work in the big house, they retire to almshouses.
sentences.zh: 从你的书中确实能感觉到，那些在这些宅邸工作的仆人，他们在庄园里长大，去大宅里工作，最后在救济院养老。

sentences.en: I mean, they are living their lives entirely framed by the great house, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们的一生完全被这座大宅所框定，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what's interesting about it is that it is both, in a sense, a rather privileged kind of job to have.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，从某种意义上说，这既是一份相当优越的工作。

sentences.en: Once you've got your feet under the table, as people used to say, you know, about their daughters, to try and get their feet under the table of the big house,
sentences.zh: 正如人们过去常说的那样，一旦你站稳了脚跟，就像他们为了让女儿能在大户人家站稳脚跟所做的那样，

sentences.en: you ate better than you had never, ever eaten before.
sentences.zh: 你就能吃到从未吃过的美味佳肴。

sentences.en: You were fairly looked after.
sentences.zh: 你会得到相当不错的照顾。

sentences.en: You were fairly comfortable.
sentences.zh: 你当时过得还算舒适。

sentences.en: You would certainly be more comfortable than you'd be at home.
sentences.zh: 你肯定会比在自己家里过得更舒服。

sentences.en: But of course, you weren't free.
sentences.zh: 但当然，你并不自由。

sentences.en: I mean, the rules about followers, for example,
sentences.zh: 我是说，比如关于随从的那些规矩，

sentences.en: I mean, the chances of getting married if you worked in a big house were probably greater than if you worked in a middle class house because you met more men
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在大户人家工作，结婚的机会可能比在中产阶级家庭工作要多，因为你能见到更多的男性，

sentences.en: because there were male servants in the household and visiting male servants.
sentences.zh: 因为家里有男仆，还有来访的男仆。

sentences.en: But still, it was frowned on.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，这种事还是不被允许的。

sentences.en: And if you did get married, you'd probably be sacked.
sentences.zh: 而且如果你真的结婚了，很可能会被解雇。

sentences.en: So it's like a sort of unmarried priestly caste looking after this inner sanctum of the family.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一个未婚的祭司阶层，守护着这个家庭的圣地。

sentences.en: But we're not talking about a niche thing, are we?
sentences.zh: 但我们谈论的并不是什么小众现象，对吧？

sentences.en: So to pull the camera right back,
sentences.zh: 所以，把镜头拉远来看，

sentences.en: Sir Tom started with his extraordinary
sentences.zh: 汤姆爵士从他那非凡的

sentences.en: Downton Abbey rendition.
sentences.zh: 《唐顿庄园》演绎开始说起。

sentences.en: And that starts, I think, in the aftermath of the sinking of the Titanic, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想那是从泰坦尼克号沉没之后开始的，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's Edwardian.
sentences.zh: 所以那是爱德华时代。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the Edwardian period is the one, it's the upstairs-downstairs world for older listeners.
sentences.zh: 对于年长的听众来说，爱德华时代就是那个“楼上楼下”的世界。

sentences.en: It's what we regard as the sort of, you know, the high point, I suppose, of the master-servant relationship.
sentences.zh: 我想，那被我们视为主人与仆人关系发展的巅峰时期。

sentences.en: And at that point, you say in your book,
sentences.zh: 而在那个节点，正如你在书中所说，

sentences.en: there are one and a half million servants in Britain, which is the single largest occupational group.
sentences.zh: 英国有一百五十万名仆人，这是单一最大的职业群体。

sentences.en: There are more servants than there are anything else.
sentences.zh: 仆人的数量比任何其他职业都要多。

sentences.en: And that's an extraordinary fact.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非同寻常的事实。

sentences.en: I think that's women, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想那是针对女性的，对吧？

sentences.en: There are more, it's for women occupational groups, certainly.
sentences.zh: 确实，在女性职业群体中，仆人的数量是最多的。

sentences.en: I've got a stat here, because I copied this out.
sentences.zh: 我这里有个数据，因为我把它抄下来了。

sentences.en: In 1900, domestic service was the single largest occupation in Edwardian Britain.
sentences.zh: 1900年，家政服务是爱德华时代英国单一最大的职业。

sentences.en: Of the four million women in the British workforce, a million and a half worked as servants.
sentences.zh: 在英国四百万女性劳动力中，有一百五十万人从事仆人工作。

sentences.en: But of course, by the time the Edwardian, the sort of acme, as Dominic was saying, the sort of acme of what we see as the kind of the great estates, the great country house,
sentences.zh: 但当然，到了爱德华时代，正如多米尼克所说，在我们所见的那些大庄园、大乡间别墅的鼎盛时期，

sentences.en: servanted households, they were already on the decline.
sentences.zh: 那些拥有仆人的家庭，其实已经在走下坡路了。

sentences.en: They'd sort of peaked and they were struggling to hold on.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎已经达到了顶峰，正在努力维持现状。

sentences.en: And having servants and having very ostentatious servants was part of a way in which you showed that you were hanging on because already women were beginning
sentences.zh: 拥有仆人，尤其是拥有非常显眼的仆人，是你展示自己仍在坚持的一种方式，因为当时女性已经开始

sentences.en: not to want to go into service because they had so many other choices.
sentences.zh: 不想再去做仆人了，因为她们有了很多其他的选择。

sentences.en: The job opportunities were expanding for women.
sentences.zh: 女性的就业机会正在扩大。

sentences.en: Well, you see that even in Downton Abbey, don't you think, Tom?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你在《唐顿庄园》里也能看到这一点，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Right from the beginning, it's a world embattled by change.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，那就是一个被变革所困扰的世界。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the detail in your book at the beginning, which you open with, is the idea that actually the superfluity, if you're very, very wealthy, if you're very, very entitled,
sentences.zh: 但你在书开头提到的细节，也就是你开篇所写的内容，是关于这种多余感，如果你非常有钱，如果你非常有权势，

sentences.en: is the entire point.
sentences.zh: 这本身就是重点所在。

sentences.en: And there are so, you know, no one ever says, oh, we've got too many servants.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，从来没有人会说，哦，我们的仆人太多了。

sentences.en: They just kind of invent strange titles for them.
sentences.zh: 他们只是给仆人发明一些奇怪的头衔。

sentences.en: And you have the brilliant details of the incapacity
sentences.zh: 你书中关于那种无能的精彩细节，

sentences.en: of even kind of brilliant men like Lord Curzon to cope with the lack of servants.
sentences.zh: 即使是像寇松勋爵这样才华横溢的人，也无法应对缺乏仆人的情况。

sentences.en: Oh, there was lots of stories of, you know, people, you know, a log, someone needs a log on the fire and they're sitting right next to it and their foot is an inch away
sentences.zh: 哦，有很多这样的故事，你知道，有人需要往火炉里添根木柴，他们就坐在火炉旁边，脚离木柴篮子只有一英寸远，

sentences.en: from the log basket, but they still ring a footman to come and do it for them.
sentences.zh: 但他们还是会叫男仆过来帮他们做这件事。

sentences.en: Do you remember the story of Lord Curzon?
sentences.zh: 你还记得关于寇松勋爵的故事吗？

sentences.en: There were many stories told about Lord Curzon, but he was, you know, as you know, supposed to be tremendously clever.
sentences.zh: 关于寇松勋爵的故事有很多，但正如你所知，他被认为是非常聪明的。

sentences.en: But he was staying in a country house and the servants had gone to bed and he couldn't open his bedroom window.
sentences.zh: 但他有一次住在乡间别墅里，仆人们都去睡觉了，他却打不开卧室的窗户。

sentences.en: He didn't know how to open the bedroom window.
sentences.zh: 他不知道怎么打开卧室的窗户。

sentences.en: So he simply picked up a log and smashed it.
